end.parentNote: Aryan practised telling points, line segments, lines and rays apart using endpoints, arrows, and the torch-light example. They correctly explained that a segment has two endpoints and a ray starts at one point and continues in one direction. Aryan first treated a longer drawn line as a different line, but this was corrected later by revisiting that a line has no endpoints and extends both ways; identifying named points in a drawing still needed support. At home, draw one example of each figure and ask Aryan to mark endpoints, arrows, and any named points.
